submitted.rationale: Index 61 (Cr 0.08, Fe 0.41, V 0.51) had the highest measured EQE, 0.77%. EQE rose from the Fe-rich sample to the Fe-V midpoint to this higher-V, lower-Cr sample. MEGNet gap predictions (about 2.7 eV, HSE and GLLB) for the queried phase are consistent with absorption at 3.2 eV.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.28% EQE; more Cr and less V than index 61.
Measured 0.15% EQE; the Fe-rich, hematite-like end performed worst.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gap of 2.75 eV for the queried Fe-V oxide phase is below the 3.2 eV photon energy, so absorption is possible. Index 90 (Fe0.46 V0.44 Cr0.10) is near the FeVO4 stoichiometry with light Cr alloying, a plausible photoanode region.

Mildly supportive: MEGNet HSE gap of ~2.77 eV for mp-19770 (which I take to be the Fe2O3 phase) is below 3.2 eV, so the sample should absorb. The Fe-rich corner (index 167, Fe 0.71) is an unexplored region distinct from index 90, so measuring it tests the hematite-like end.

Supportive: the GLLB gap of about 2.7 eV agrees with the HSE value, so this phase should absorb at 3.2 eV. EQE fell from 0.28% at index 90 to 0.15% at the Fe-rich index 167. Index 61 moves the other way, to higher V and lower Cr, and is one of the GP top-5 candidates.
